title: Inkling by Thinking Machines
hook: Thinking Machines' open-weight multimodal MoE reads image, text, and audio in a 1-million-token context — and skips RoPE for relative position encoding instead.
key_points: Decoder-only Mixture-of-Experts: 975B total parameters, 41B active, routing top-6 of 256 experts plus 2 always-on shared experts.
Natively multimodal — processes image, text, and audio together, with a 1-million-token context window.
Hybrid attention alternates global and sliding-window layers 5:1; uses relative, distance-based position encoding instead of RoPE.
Adds short convolution layers for local representations, kept separate from the attention mechanism.
Scores 77.6% on SWE-Bench Verified, 87.2% on GPQA Diamond, 91.4% on VoiceBench; strong on vision reasoning and multilingual audio.
Ships open-weight in full precision (2TB VRAM) and smaller quantized variants, supported across major inference frameworks.
content_html: Thinking Machines released Inkling, an open-weight, natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model that reads image, text, and audio together in a single 1-million-token context. Structurally, it departs from the now-standard RoPE-and-dense-attention playbook on several fronts.
extra_html: Inkling activates 41B of its 975B total parameters per token, spread across 256 experts (top-6 routed, plus 2 shared experts always on). Attention alternates global and sliding-window layers in a 5:1 ratio, and swaps RoPE for a relative, distance-based scheme learned directly in the attention logits; short convolution layers add local representation kept separate from attention. Reported scores include 77.6% on SWE-Bench Verified, 87.2% on GPQA Diamond, and 91.4% on VoiceBench, alongside strong vision-reasoning and multilingual audio results. It ships open-weight — full precision needs 2TB of VRAM, with smaller quantized variants available — and is supported across major inference frameworks, per Thinking Machines' release post.

related.title: Mixtral of Experts
related.hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.

flashcards.prompt: How big is Inkling, and how much of it is active per token?
flashcards.back_html: 975B total parameters, but only 41B are active per token — the router picks top-6 of 256 experts plus 2 shared experts that are always on.

flashcards.prompt: What positional encoding does Inkling use instead of the common RoPE approach?

choices.text: Relative, distance-based position encoding learned directly in attention logits
Standard RoPE, same as most modern LLMs

flashcards.explanation_html: Inkling learns position directly in attention logits via a relative feature based on distance between query and key, rather than RoPE.

flashcards.prompt: What's distinctive about Inkling's attention pattern across layers?
flashcards.back_html: It alternates full-context (global) attention and sliding-window attention in a 5:1 ratio, mixing long-range and local attention layers.

flashcards.prompt: Besides text and images, what other modality does Inkling natively process?
flashcards.explanation_html: Inkling natively handles image, text, and audio inputs within its 1-million-token context window.
